examples.name: Standalone radio
examples.description: A single labeled radio outside a group.

examples.name: Label-less table radio
examples.description: Row selection where the row content already provides visible context, described instead by aria-label.
examples.jsx: <Radio aria-label="Select primary matter" name="matter-radio" value="primary" defaultChecked />

examples.name: Controlled RadioGroup
examples.description: Single selection driven by external state via the options API.
examples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" value={value} onValueChange={setValue} options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }, { value: 'mail', label: 'Mail' }]} />

examples.name: Uncontrolled RadioGroup
examples.description: Single selection with an initial value, owned by the native fieldset.
examples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Delivery speed" name="delivery-speed" defaultValue="standard" options={[{ value: 'standard', label: 'Standard' }, { value: 'expedited', label: 'Expedited' }, { value: 'overnight', label: 'Overnight' }]} />

examples.name: RadioGroup with children composition
examples.description: A custom layout of manually-wired Radio instances, used instead of the options API.
examples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Status" name="status" description="Grouped manually instead of using the options API"><Radio label="Draft" name="status" value="draft" defaultChecked /><Radio label="In review" name="status" value="in-review" /><Radio label="Final" name="status" value="final" /></RadioGroup>

props.label: Status
props.name: status
props.description: Grouped manually instead of using the options API

examples.name: Horizontal orientation
examples.description: Options laid out in a row that wraps rather than overflowing.
examples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Delivery speed" name="delivery-speed" orientation="horizontal" defaultValue="standard" options={[{ value: 'standard', label: 'Standard' }, { value: 'expedited', label: 'Expedited' }, { value: 'overnight', label: 'Overnight' }]} />

examples.name: Required RadioGroup
examples.description: A required group-level question, with the indicator shown after the legend.
examples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" required options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

examples.name: Invalid RadioGroup with error message
examples.description: Invalid state paired with a visible, described error rather than color alone.
examples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" invalid errorMessage="Choose one option before continuing." options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

examples.name: Disabled RadioGroup
examples.description: Every generated option is disabled together.
examples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" disabled defaultValue="email" options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

antiExamples.name: Loose radios wired by hand
antiExamples.jsx:
<Radio name="method" value="email" label="Email" checked={method === 'email'} onCheckedChange={() => setMethod('email')} />
<Radio name="method" value="phone" label="Phone" checked={method === 'phone'} onCheckedChange={() => setMethod('phone')} />
antiExamples.reason: The set has no legend, and every radio needs its own name and checked logic. Use RadioGroup's options, which shares the name and keeps the value for you.

antiExamples.name: Marking one option required
antiExamples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email', required: true }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />
antiExamples.reason: The browser still asks for an answer, but the * looks as if only that option is required. Set required on the group, which puts the * after the legend.

antiExamples.name: Invalid with no message
antiExamples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" invalid options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />
antiExamples.reason: The red circles alone don't say what's wrong, and not everyone can see the color. Pair invalid with an errorMessage that explains the problem.

antiExamples.name: Radios for independent choices
antiExamples.jsx: <RadioGroup label="Send matter updates by" options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'sms', label: 'SMS' }]} />
antiExamples.reason: Radios allow exactly one answer. When any number of options can apply, use Checkbox (Checkbox Group).

antiExamples.name: No accessible name
antiExamples.reason: Without label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby the radio is announced with no name. Name a label-less radio, such as one in a table row, with aria-label.
